stem: The graph models the population, in thousands, of a town x years since 2004, where 0 ≤ x ≤ 15. Which statement is the best interpretation of the point (1, 5.30)?

choices.label: A
choices.content: In 2019, the estimated population of the town was 5,300.

choices.label: B
choices.content: In 2018, the estimated population of the town was 5,300.

choices.label: C
choices.content: In 2005, the estimated population of the town was 5,300.

choices.label: D
choices.content: In 2004, the estimated population of the town was 5,300.

whyCorrect: Read the two coordinates against the units the stem defines. The first coordinate is x, measured in years since 2004, so x = 1 means 2004 + 1 = 2005. The second coordinate is population in thousands, so 5.30 means 5.30 thousand = 5,300 people.

whyWrong.A: 2019 is 15 years after 2004, which is x = 15, the right-hand end of the domain, not x = 1.
whyWrong.B: 2018 is 14 years after 2004, so it corresponds to x = 14. The point's first coordinate is 1.
whyWrong.D: 2004 itself is x = 0, the starting year. x = 1 is one year later.

note: The graph is shown for context, but the point (1, 5.30) is stated in the stem, so the interpretation follows from the units alone.

stem: The function f is defined by \( f(x) = 8 + \sqrt{x} \) . What is the value of \( f(36) \) ?
whyCorrect: Substitute 36 for x. The square root of 36 is 6, so \( f(36) = 8 + 6 = 14 \) . The 8 is added after the root is taken, not inside it.

whyWrong.A: 0 would require \( \sqrt{36} = -8 \) . You may have set the output equal to 0 and tried to solve instead of substituting the input.
whyWrong.C: 17 is 8 + 9, which treats the square root of 36 as 9. 9 is the square root of 81; \( 6^2 = 36 \) .
whyWrong.D: 26 is 8 + 18, which halves 36 instead of taking its square root.

stem: The graph of \( y = f(x) \) is shown in the xy-plane. What is the value of \( f(0) \) ?
whyCorrect: \( f(0) \) is the output when the input is 0, so look at where the curve meets the y-axis (the vertical line x = 0). The curve crosses the y-axis at 5, so \( f(0) = 5 \) .

whyWrong.B: -6 is a y-value on the lower right branch of the curve, which sits at positive x. Nothing there has an input of 0.
whyWrong.C: -2 is roughly where the lower branch levels off far to the right; it is a value the curve approaches for large x, not the value at x = 0.
whyWrong.D: 4 reads the crossing one gridline too low. The curve is at 4 slightly to the left of the y-axis, and it is still rising when it reaches x = 0.
